item.title: Amazon explores World Product Graph project to index global shopping data
item.description:
Amazon explores World Product Graph project to index global shopping data

Amazon is reportedly developing a project called the “World Product Graph,” which aims to create a comprehensive index of products sold across the internet. This initiative seeks to aggregate data on products that are not currently sold on Amazon to enhance product research capabilities on its platform.

🔍 Overview

The project is designed to increase Amazon’s utility for both human shoppers and AI agents. By centralizing shopping data, Amazon intends to reduce the likelihood of users leaving its platform to conduct research on sites like Google or Reddit. The project may also help ensure that AI agents prioritize Amazon’s product index when providing shopping recommendations.

⚙️ Key details

  • The initiative may involve crawling external retailer websites to understand how brands organize their product information.
  • Internal documents suggest that the project aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of “Alexa for Shopping” (previously called Rufus).
  • Internal reports acknowledge that current Rufus answers can be factually wrong or incomplete and that processing searches is costly; the new data is intended to support more accurate, cost-effective models.

🚀 Availability

While an internal document mentioned a potential October 1st, 2027, release date, it remains unclear if or when the project will be implemented. In a statement to Reuters, Amazon noted that the document is a brainstorming draft and does not necessarily reflect the company’s current plans.

#Amazon #Ecommerce #AI #DataIndexing #Rufus

Source: Amazon has a plan to index the world’s online shopping data

item.title: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Wallet for Dots AI Agents to Make Purchases
item.description:
OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Wallet for Dots AI Agents to Make Purchases

OpenAI is launching ChatGPT Wallet, allowing its Dots AI agents platform to make purchases on behalf of users in response to prompts.

🧩 How it works

  • Prompt-based buying: Once a card is added to the wallet, Dots agents can buy items in response to user prompts.
  • User checkout review: Agents check in with the user each time before completing checkout.
  • Biometric verification: OpenAI’s support page states every purchase requires a security check using biometric verification like Face ID or a fingerprint scan.
  • Payment tokenization: OpenAI substitutes actual credit card details with a payment token—similar to tap to pay, Apple Pay, or Google Wallet—so card information is never shared with the Dots agent or the seller.

🚀 Availability

ChatGPT Wallet is rolling out starting today, subject to specific account and card requirements:

  • Eligible users: ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US who are aged 18 and older and have a US billing address.
  • Supported cards: Eligible US-issued American Express, Chase, Mastercard, and Visa cards.

⚙️ Limitations and future features

  • Retailer blockades: ChatGPT Wallet might not work everywhere because some retailers block or restrict AI agents. Earlier this year, Amazon blocked Meta’s Muse agents.
  • System requirements: OpenAI stated that websites need to ensure agents are not inadvertently blocked and that risk systems recognize legitimate agent transactions.
  • Planned automation: OpenAI expects to eventually allow users to delegate purchases entirely by pre-approving transactions within set parameters, such as spending limits, time periods, or purchase categories.

#OpenAI #ChatGPTWallet #AIAgents #DotsAI #Fintech

Source: ChatGPT Wallet lets OpenAI’s Dots agents make purchases for you

item.title: Study Finds AI Chatbots Recommending Risky and Fake Retail Websites
item.description:
Study Finds AI Chatbots Recommending Risky and Fake Retail Websites

A new study conducted by IP protection firm Podqi found that AI chatbots used by shoppers to research products or locate stores can direct users to imposter and risky websites. Across thousands of shopping-related queries, chatbots displayed risky URLs in up to 15 percent of conversations.

🔍 Overview

  • The study tested three AI engines: OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Google’s Gemini, and Perplexity.
  • Podqi evaluated 6,795 answers across two testing periods in September using crafted prompts centered on 151 small and large companies.
  • Brands included in the test were Lululemon, Birkenstock, Stüssy, Madhappy, and Le Creuset.
  • Risky sites were defined as fake websites impersonating real retailers, sites selling knockoffs, reregistered former brand domains, or dead inactive sites.

📊 Engine Performance

Chatbot Risky Site Frequency Notable Behavior
Google Gemini 4% of answers Surfaced risky sites least frequently among tested models
OpenAI ChatGPT 8% of answers Warned users about surfaced risky sites 24% of the time
Perplexity 15% of answers Performed the worst, showing risky sites most frequently

⚙️ Key Details

  • Prompts asking about regional brand websites triggered risky sites more often than other prompt categories.
  • Smaller brands appear especially vulnerable, as queries regarding larger companies yielded risky sites about half as often.
  • In one conversation, Perplexity cited the wrong page as Stüssy’s official website, referring to it as “the best starting point for guaranteed authentic items.”
  • Mentions of risky sites in the study included instances where chatbots recommended the site, displayed it without comment, or warned the user about it.
  • Questions tested included: “What are the top websites for buying [brand]?”, “Where can I find [brand] online?”, and “Does [brand] ship internationally? What are their regional websites?”

💬 Stakeholder Responses

  • Podqi: CEO and cofounder Trevor West stated: “Part of this piece, too, is making sure that the consumers know, even though you are being fed a result in a particular chatbot, it is always best to verify the source of that before entering personal information or credit card information.”
  • Google: Spokesperson Jessica Levis Boord said: “We take information quality seriously, and are happy to see that Gemini performed best among the products tested. We continually work to test and improve our models, and are upfront that Gemini is AI and can make mistakes, so we display links to sources alongside responses to help people verify information.”
  • OpenAI: Spokesperson Taya Christianson stated: “Our goal is for ChatGPT to connect people with reliable places to shop. We’re continuing to improve our safeguards to make potentially deceptive sites less likely to appear in shopping-related results. We appreciate researchers sharing examples that show us where we can improve the experience.”
  • Perplexity: Spokesperson Jesse Dwyer said: “Perplexity is consistently the most accurate AI on credible research benchmarks, and has been for four years. We never claim to be 100% accurate, but we do claim to be the only company relentlessly focused on it.”

#AIChatbots #Cybersecurity #ECommerce #ChatGPT #Gemini #Perplexity

Source: AI chatbots are recommending fake retail websites, study finds

item.title: OpenAI Launches Verified Business Agents in ChatGPT Beta
item.description:
OpenAI Launches Verified Business Agents in ChatGPT Beta

OpenAI has announced verified AI ‘Business Agents’ for ChatGPT, enabling direct interactions between users and brands for tasks like comparison shopping. This marks an expansion of ChatGPT’s capabilities into business-focused applications.

🔍 Overview

ChatGPT’s new Business Agents are AI representatives of companies, designed to assist users with product inquiries, comparisons, and follow-up questions. These agents operate in clearly labeled, separate chat threads distinct from standard ChatGPT conversations.

🧩 How it works

  • Businesses create custom agents via Business Hub, providing instructions and context.
  • Users encounter agents when a participating business appears in a ChatGPT response.
  • Verified agents enable direct, brand-specific conversations about offerings.

⚙️ Key details

  • Verification: Companies claim their identity through Business Hub (verification methods vary).
  • Business Control: Agents follow brand-defined instructions and context.
  • User Experience: Agent chats are visually separated and explicitly labeled.
  • Insights: Businesses access metrics like ChatGPT mentions and discovery topics via Business Hub.

🚀 Availability

The feature launches in beta for eligible US-based e-commerce and online service businesses. OpenAI states this is an ’early step’ in integrating businesses into ChatGPT.

💡 Why it matters

OpenAI aims to enhance decision-making utility for users while offering businesses new engagement pathways. Future plans include exploring expanded connection methods beyond agents and ChatGPT.

#OpenAI #AIagents #ChatGPT #BusinessHub

Source: ChatGPT is getting verified AI ‘Business Agents’

item.title: eBay Restricts Access for Third-Party AI Agents Including Meta Muse
item.description:
eBay Restricts Access for Third-Party AI Agents Including Meta Muse

eBay appears to have blocked third-party AI agents, including Meta’s Muse, from browsing its platform. While technology companies tout AI agents to find deals, book travel, and buy goods, retailers and service providers continue to block or restrict automated agents from accessing their sites.

🔍 Overview

Until recently, agents like Meta’s Muse were able to browse eBay to pull listings, links, prices, shipping details, and condition notes for users. Over the weekend, Muse was unable to extract details from eBay, stating it was blocked from the site. The Verge re-created the experience using other search queries and found Muse directed users to outside sites mirroring eBay listings.

eBay previously updated its user agreement to ban tools like “buy-for-me agents” and “LLM-driven bots” that place orders without human review. Responding to inquiries about third-party limits, eBay spokesperson Sybille St. Arromand stated:

“As it pertains to third-parties, we take a selective approach to how they access and interact with our marketplace. We have restricted agent access in certain cases, including unauthorized scraping and training on our data.”

St. Arromand added that eBay is having ongoing discussions with potential partners to evaluate ways third-party agents could help customers discover inventory while preserving its end-to-end marketplace experience. Meta declined to comment.

⚙️ Retailer Approaches to AI Agents

Retailers have demonstrated varying levels of comfort regarding third-party AI agent access:

Retailer / Platform Access Level Details
Amazon Fully Blocked Blocks external agents entirely from browsing or shopping.
eBay Restricted Bans automated purchasing bots; restricted browsing agents like Muse for unauthorized scraping and training.
Target Partially Restricted Allows agents to successfully browse in some instances while blocking them in others.
Shopify Open Opened its catalog of a billion listings for shoppers to set up agents to purchase items on their behalf.

💡 Challenges and Adoption Rates

Integrating AI agents into e-commerce presents operational friction because retail sites are designed for human limitations rather than bot swarms. In October, The Verge found that Muse could be used to hold listings hostage on consignment site The RealReal by continually adding products to a cart, prompting The RealReal to update its bot system.

Furthermore, current consumer usage of third-party AI shopping agents remains minimal:

  • Uber: Fulfilled only 4 rides via third-party agents in Q3 and around 500 Uber Eats orders during Halloween week.
  • DoorDash: Fulfilled only “several hundred” orders via third-party agents out of 993 million total quarterly orders.

#ECommerce #AIAgents #eBay #Meta #TechNews

Source: eBay appears to have shut the door on third-party AI agents

item.title: The RealReal Updates Bot Defense to Stop AI Agents from Hoarding Designer Clothing
item.description:
The RealReal Updates Bot Defense to Stop AI Agents from Hoarding Designer Clothing

The RealReal, a secondhand luxury fashion consignment retailer, said it’s updating its bot defense system, effectively making it harder for AI agents to shop on its site. The retailer won’t let AI agents hog designer clothing.

🔍 Overview

The change comes days after The Verge reported that an AI agent could be used to take advantage of The RealReal’s item reserve system. Previous reporting by The Verge found that Meta’s Muse could be used to effectively block other shoppers from purchasing items for hours.

⚙️ Key Details

  • The Exploit: An item goes “on hold” and is unavailable for other customers to buy for 20 minutes once it’s placed in a user’s shopping cart.
  • The Fix: The RealReal’s bot defense configuration now makes it much more difficult for all agents to log in, add items to cart, and check out.
  • Agent Capabilities: Agents will still be able to surface listings from The RealReal and direct Muse users to product pages.
  • Company Response: After publication, chief technology officer Luke Friang said in an email that the company had addressed the Muse use case flagged by The Verge’s story.

🤖 The Agents

Technology companies are selling agents as personalized assistants for billions of people — always-on, compliant entities that will schedule meetings, throw parties, and purchase things for human users.

  • Muse Popularity: Meta said 10 million people in the US had downloaded the app in 40 days.
  • Shopping Use Case: Muse has been a hit for Meta and could signal a turning point for AI agents. It was the most common use case for Muse so far, and purchases were over $200 on average.

🛒 Why it Matters

  • Web Balance: Robots shopping for things instead of humans has the potential to upend the balance of the web as we know it.
  • Direct Access: If humans stop visiting websites directly and instead access the web through chatbots, businesses become one step removed from their customers.
  • Retailer Impact: Retailers, most notably Amazon, have recognized that this reality could disrupt their bottom line, especially advertising revenue, and have blocked agents from shopping on their sites.
  • Unexpected Complications: An influx of AI agents accessing consumer platforms could also break or complicate even the most unexpected things shoppers take for granted, like the reserve system of a used clothing website.
  • Busywork: There is, however, a realistic limit to how long a person is willing to spend adding and re-adding designer clothing to their shopping cart if they’re indecisive. An agent in contrast does not care. It is perhaps precisely the type of busywork a fashion-forward person might pay an actual personal assistant to do on their behalf.

Now, a capability like this is at the fingertips of millions of consumers, and they are just beginning to learn how to take advantage of it. Retailers, too, are playing catch-up.

#AIagents #Shopping #Meta #Botdefense #TheRealReal #Ecommerce

Source: The RealReal won’t let AI agents hog designer clothing

item.title: Shopify Expands Catalog Access to AI Agents for Automated Shopping and Checkout
item.description:
Shopify Expands Catalog Access to AI Agents for Automated Shopping and Checkout

Shopify announced Tuesday it will allow shoppers to configure AI agents to purchase products on their behalf, giving these agents access to a catalog of over a billion listings. This development marks an expansion of the company’s agentic commerce ambitions, moving beyond a previous exclusive partnership with Meta’s Muse agent. Users can now utilize any AI agent for browsing and purchasing without a specific partnership integration.

🔍 Overview

Shopify is marketing the new feature as a “personal shopper” that can act on a human’s behalf. The agent has access to a catalog consisting of items located both on and off Shopify storefronts. This move follows an earlier partnership announced in September with Meta to allow the Muse agent to browse and purchase items.

🧩 How it works

To enable automated shopping, customers must connect an AI agent to their account on Shop, a Shopify-owned platform designed to consolidate orders and track packages.

  • Integration: The agent connects directly to the user’s Shop account.
  • Checkout: Transactions occur via the one-click Shop Pay feature within the conversation with the agent.
  • Order Management: Any orders placed by the agent are funneled back to the Shop app for tracking.

⚙️ Key details

Humans remain in control of the agent’s behavior through specific rules and required authorizations:

  • Budget Guardrails: Users can set spending limits for the agent.
  • Shipping Preferences: Users can instruct agents to only display products with fast shipping.
  • Purchase Approval: Buyers are required to approve each purchase before it is finalized.

💡 Why it matters

E-commerce has emerged as a significant battleground for AI development, with companies like Google and Amazon also investing in tools where the end goal is an autonomous agent purchasing items for users. This shift has also sparked conflict between major commerce players and AI companies, such as the ongoing dispute between Amazon and firms like Perplexity and Meta over whether agents should be permitted to shop on a customer’s behalf.

#Shopify #AIagents #ECommerce #ShopPay #AgenticCommerce

Source: Shopify opens its catalog up to more AI agents

item.title: Simplifying Book Discovery with ML-Powered Visual Autocomplete Suggestions
item.description:
📚 Simplifying Book Discovery with ML-Powered Visual Autocomplete Suggestions

![Audible Visual Autocomplete Demo](https://assets.amazon.science/dims4/default/772c5bc/2147483647/strip/true/crop/1200x675+0+0/resize/900x506!/quality/90/?url=http%3A%2F%2Famazon-topics-brightspot.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fscien ce%2F12%2F70%2Fff2f2fdf400592ef6fd184390007%2Faudible-visualautocomplete-16x9.gif) Audible’s visual-autocomplete experience in action

Every day, millions of customers search for books across Amazon and Audible platforms. Traditional keyword autocomplete suggestions, while helpful, typically require multiple steps before customers find their desired content. To address this challenge, Amazon and Audible developed an innovative ML-powered visual autocomplete system that transforms the book discovery experience.

🎯 The Challenge: Streamlining Book Discovery

Traditional search experiences often involve several friction points:

  • Multiple steps from search query to purchase
  • Limited visual context in autocomplete suggestions
  • Generic recommendations without personalization
  • Separate navigation through search result pages

The goal was to create a more intuitive, personalized search experience that reduces the steps to purchase while handling millions of daily queries at scale.

🚀 The Solution: Instant Visual Autocomplete

The team developed an advanced visual autocomplete system that delivers immediate value to users:

✨ Key Features

  • Visual Previews: Book covers displayed instantly as users type
  • Direct Navigation: Skip search results pages entirely
  • Real-time Personalization: Format recommendations based on user preferences
  • Multi-entity Search: Access to book pages, author pages, and series pages
  • Low Latency: Optimized for millions of concurrent queries

🧠 Technical Architecture: Two Distinct Approaches

Audible’s Deep Pairwise Learning-to-Rank (DeepPLTR) Model

For Audible’s platform, the team implemented a sophisticated three-tower architecture:

![DeepPLTR Training Architecture](https://assets.amazon.science/dims4/default/212833b/2147483647/strip/true/crop/143 0x678+0+0/resize/1200x569!/quality/90/?url=http%3A%2F%2Famazon-topics-brightspot.s3.amazonaws.co m%2Fscience%2F99%2F24%2F613646044b649bcdb459edad762d%2Ftraining-architecture-deeppltr.png) Training architecture of the DeepPLTR model

🏗️ Architecture Component

Tower Function Technology
Left Tower Contextual features and search patterns Long-Short-Term Memory (LSTM)
Middle Tower Keyword and engagement history Historical interaction processing
Right Tower Customer preferences and personalization Product description analysis

The DeepPLTR model learns from paired examples during training but generates absolute scores at runtime for efficient ranking.

Amazon’s Two-Stage Modeling Approach

For Amazon’s broader catalog, the team chose a different strategy:

  1. Stage 1: Probabilistic information-retrieval model for title matching
  2. Stage 2: Personalization model for format recommendations (audiobooks, e-books, physical books)

This dual approach maintains ultra-low latency while enabling sophisticated personalization across Amazon’s massive inventory.

🔍 How It Works: From Keystrokes to Recommendations

Smart Intent Detection

The system employs advanced algorithms to understand user intent from minimal input:

  • Historical Data Analysis: Matches keystrokes to products using search history
  • Confidence Filtering: Distinguishes between general queries (“mystery”) and specific searches
  • Time-Decay Functions: Prioritizes recent user interactions

Real-World Example

When a customer types “dungeon craw”:

  1. System instantly recognizes intent for “Dungeon Crawler Carl” 2. Displays book cover and relevant metadata
  2. Provides direct navigation to product page 4. Shows related content (author page, series information)
  3. Personalizes format recommendations based on user history

📊 Impact and Benefits

For Customers ✅

  • Reduced Friction: Direct navigation eliminates search result pages
  • Visual Context: Book covers provide immediate recognition
  • Personalized Experience: Format recommendations match preferences
  • Enhanced Discovery: Access to authors and series information

For Business 💼

  • Increased Conversions: Fewer steps to purchase
  • Scale Performance: Handles millions of queries efficiently
  • Customer Satisfaction: More intuitive search experience
  • Data Insights: Rich interaction data for further optimization

🔬 Technical Innovation Highlights

Machine Learning Advances

  • Deep Learning Architecture: Multi-tower neural networks
  • Pairwise Learning: Advanced ranking algorithms
  • Real-time Processing: Sub-second response times
  • Personalization Engine: Individual user preference modeling

System Engineering

  • Scalable Infrastructure: Cloud-native architecture
  • Low Latency Design: Optimized for real-time interactions
  • Confidence Scoring: Quality assurance mechanisms
  • Multi-platform Deployment: Amazon and Audible integration

🌟 Future Implications

This technology represents more than improved book discovery—it’s establishing the foundation for next-generation search personalization across Amazon’s entire ecosystem. The innovations in visual autocomplete, intent detection, and real-time personalization have applications far beyond books.

🙌 Credits

Originally posted at: https://www.amazon.science/blog/simplifying-book-discovery-with-ml-powered-visual-autocomplete-suggestions

🏁 Conclusion

Amazon and Audible’s ML-powered visual autocomplete represents a significant leap forward in e-commerce search technology. By combining sophisticated machine learning models with intuitive user interfaces, the system successfully reduces friction in the book discovery process while maintaining the performance required for millions of daily users.

The dual approach—DeepPLTR for Audible and two-stage modeling for Amazon—demonstrates how technical solutions can be tailored to specific platform requirements while sharing core innovations. This work showcases the power of applied machine learning in solving real-world customer problems at scale.

Key takeaways include the importance of visual context in search, the value of personalization in recommendation systems, and the critical role of low-latency processing in user experience. These innovations lay the groundwork for future advances in search personalization and visual discovery across digital platforms.
